papers.title: Drug Repositioning in Kinase Inhibitor Discovery for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: Repurposing of existing drugs has emerged as a time- and cost-effective strategy in oncology drug discovery. Given the critical role of dysregulated kinase signaling in cancer, kinase-focused repurposing strategies have attracted considerable interest. This approach encompasses both "target hopping" between different kinases and the discovery of unexpected kinase inhibitory activity in non-kinase drugs. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the repositioning of kinase inhibitors from medicinal chemistry and structural biology perspectives. We highlight the structural basis and bindin
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent strategies for repurposing existing drugs as kinase inhibitors for cancer therapy, covering both 'target hopping' between kinases and the discovery of unexpected kinase-inhibitory activity in non-kinase drugs. It emphasizes medicinal chemistry and structural biology perspectives, highlighting binding mechanisms and structural determinants that enable rational repositioning.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in myeloproliferative neoplasms: From digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders whose diagnosis, prognostication, and management depend on integrating heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data. This narrative review (PubMed/MEDLINE searched through August 2026, supplemented by hand-searching and conference abstracts) appraises the evidence for AI applications across the MPN continuum. Artificial intelligence (AI), and its principal subfields, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), learn predictive patterns directly from data rather than from explicitly programmed rules,
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys the evidence for artificial intelligence applications across the myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) continuum, from digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support. It covers how machine learning and deep learning can integrate heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data to aid diagnosis, prognostication, and management. The review is intended as a synthesis of current evidence rather than a primary study.

papers.title: LASSBio-classFLOW: A Semiautomated KNIME Workflow for Classification Model Benchmarking and Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Machine learning-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (ML-QSAR) modeling requires consistent data preparation, validation, and model comparison. We present LASSBio-classFLOW, an open, modular, and semiautomated KNIME workflow for classification-based ligand screening. It integrates basic molecular structure preparation, configurable class assignment, descriptors and fingerprints calculation, dataset partitioning, hyperparameter optimization of nine algorithms, interactive performance evaluation, user-guided model selection, and external-library prediction. As an example, the work
papers.summary: LASSBio-classFLOW is an open, modular KNIME workflow that automates the key steps of machine learning-based QSAR classification, from molecular preparation and descriptor calculation through hyperparameter optimization of nine algorithms to model evaluation and virtual screening of external libraries. It provides a semiautomated, user-guided pipeline for benchmarking classification models and applying them to ligand screening, lowering the barrier to reproducible ML-QSAR work.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning has been applied across amyloid research, from predicting amyloidogenic sequences to structural characterization and inhibitor/drug design for neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It organizes the field into sequence prediction, structural biology, and inhibitor design, highlighting ML as a unifying paradigm for amyloid investigation.

papers.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware fe
papers.summary: This study builds a computational drug discovery pipeline that combines machine learning on pathway-level features from 16 RA GEO datasets with target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro testing to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis activity. The framework uses GSVA-derived pathway features for cohort-aware modeling and reserves one dataset for independent external validation, then funnels predictions through structural and experimental filters.

papers.title: Navigating the Eukaryotic Paradox: Insights for AI-Driven Computational Strategies Against Antifungal Resistance.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of invasive fungal infections and increasing antifungal resistance demand rapid therapeutic innovation. Given the critically narrow clinical arsenal, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal strategies to accelerate drug repurposing, providing a rapid alternative to de novo drug discovery. However, translational success in medical mycology faces a major biological hurdle: the "eukaryotic paradox," the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology between fungal cells and human hosts. This review provides a critical and compara
papers.summary: This review examines how AI and machine learning can accelerate antifungal drug repurposing, while highlighting the 'eukaryotic paradox'—the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural similarity between fungal pathogens and human hosts that complicates target specificity. It critically compares computational strategies and their translational challenges in medical mycology, offering guidance for AI-driven approaches to combat rising antifungal resistance.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology.
papers.abstract: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, na
papers.summary: This review proposes a three-part taxonomy for integrating mechanistic mathematical models with artificial intelligence in the life sciences. The authors argue that mechanistic models provide explanatory depth while AI provides predictive power from high-dimensional data, and that combining them could enable more predictive and personalized biology. The paper serves as a roadmap for how these two paradigms can be synthesized.

papers.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across four areas of brucellosis research: diagnosis, genomic analysis, epidemiological prediction, and drug discovery. It highlights that traditional control strategies are limited by slow and biosafety-risky culture methods, difficulty distinguishing natural infection from vaccine-induced immunity in serology, and challenges in separating vaccine from wild-type strains via genotyping—gaps that AI approaches may help address.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase (MELK) is a cell cycle-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, and represents a promising anticancer drug target. Discovery of structurally novel, highly selective MELK inhibitors remains an unmet need. Methods: In the study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining four machine learning regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), hierarchical Glide docking (HTVS to SP to XP), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to
papers.summary: The authors combined machine learning regressors with hierarchical molecular docking, MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations to virtually screen for novel MELK kinase inhibitors. They identified a lead compound that shows antiproliferative activity and induces G2/M cell cycle arrest in triple-negative breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma cell lines. The work presents an integrated computational-to-experimental pipeline for kinase inhibitor discovery.

papers.title: Identifying Anticancer Peptide via a Semi-Supervised Prediction Framework with Bio-Inspired Augmentation.
papers.abstract: Anticancer peptides (ACPs) have emerged as a promising class of therapeutic molecules due to their low toxicity and high specificity. However, experimentally identifying ACPs is labor-intensive and low-throughput, making virtual screening with intelligent models an attractive alternative. Despite recent progress, the number of ACP samples available in existing databases remains limited, which may cause predictive models to overfit the labeled information and exhibit suboptimal generalization. To address this issue, we propose a semi-supervised prediction framework with bio-inspired data augmen
papers.summary: The authors propose a semi-supervised prediction framework for identifying anticancer peptides (ACPs) that uses bio-inspired data augmentation to address the scarcity of labeled ACP samples. By combining limited labeled data with augmented examples, the approach aims to reduce overfitting and improve generalization compared to existing ACP classifiers. This offers a computational screening alternative to labor-intensive experimental identification of therapeutic peptides.

papers.title: A Computational Workflow Integrating Explainable AI and Database Mining for the Prioritization of Antimicrobial Natural Products.
papers.abstract: The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance demands the discovery of antibacterial agents with unprecedented chemical scaffolds. Natural products have historically been the most prolific source of antibiotics, yet the vast majority of catalogued natural products remain untested for antimicrobial activity. Here we present Natural-Product Graph-language, Uncertainty-Aware Relational Discovery (NP-GUARD), a modular computational framework that reframes antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem. NP-GUARD integrates six core
papers.summary: The authors present NP-GUARD, a modular computational framework that combines explainable AI with database mining to prioritize natural products with potential antimicrobial activity. It treats antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem, integrating six core components to rank untested compounds. The work aims to help address antimicrobial resistance by surfacing promising natural-product candidates from large catalogues.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Background: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives: This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods: A literature s
papers.summary: This review surveys next-generation ALS disease models, focusing on iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems combined with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 editing, multi-omics, and AI/machine learning, and compares them with conventional in vivo and 2D in vitro platforms. It argues these integrated platforms better recapitulate ALS pathological hallmarks and could improve translational drug discovery, though the abstract is truncated and no primary data are presented.

papers.title: DeepAVPred: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating RECM-DWT and BiGRU for Accurate Antiviral Peptide Prediction.
papers.abstract: Viral infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge. Antiviral peptides (AVPs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their high specificity, favorable safety profiles, and broad-spectrum antiviral activity. However, experimental AVP identification is time-consuming and costly, while existing computational predictors often have limitations in predictive accuracy and feature representation. Here, we propose DeepAVPred, a deep learning-based framework for AVP identification. DeepAVPred integrates complementary sequence descriptors to capture physicochemical pro
papers.summary: DeepAVPred is a deep learning framework for predicting antiviral peptides from sequence alone, combining a new residue-level encoding method (RECM-DWT) with a bidirectional GRU network. The approach aims to improve on existing computational predictors that struggle with accuracy and feature representation, offering a faster alternative to costly experimental AVP identification.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Driven Identification and Experimental Validation of COX-2 and ERK1/2 as Anti-Inflammatory Targets of Avenanthramides.
papers.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation underlies numerous chronic diseases, yet the molecular targets of dietary bioactive compounds remain largely unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning to predict molecular targets of avenanthramides, oat-derived polyphenols, and experimentally validates COX-2 and ERK1/2 as anti-inflammatory targets. The work links dietary compounds to specific inflammatory pathways, supporting their potential in managing chronic low-grade inflammation.

papers.title: Correction to "PoseidonQ: A Free Machine Learning Platform for the Development, Analysis, and Validation of Efficient and Portable QSAR Models for Drug Discovery".
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for the previously published article 'PoseidonQ: A Free Machine Learning Platform for the Development, Analysis, and Validation of Efficient and Portable QSAR Models for Drug Discovery.' It does not present new scientific findings but rather corrects errors in the original publication. The underlying work describes a free machine learning platform for building portable QSAR models in drug discovery.

papers.title: Predicting Synergistic and Antagonistic Micellization Effects in Surfactant Blends for Optimized Formulation Design.
papers.abstract: Surfactant mixtures exhibit non-ideal interactions that govern their macroscopic behavior, yet their prediction is limited by the need for experimentally derived interaction parameters. Within Rubingh's Regular Solution Approximation (RST), these interactions are described by the parameter β, which is typically obtained by fitting experimental mixture data, restricting its applicability in large-scale formulation design. In this work, a computational hybrid approach combining machine learning with thermodynamic modeling is introduced to enable end-to-end prediction and optimization of surfacta
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper introduces a hybrid machine-learning and thermodynamic modeling approach that predicts the interaction parameter β for surfactant mixtures without requiring experimental fitting. This enables end-to-end prediction of synergistic or antagonistic micellization in surfactant blends, supporting large-scale formulation design. The method addresses a key bottleneck in applying regular solution theory to practical formulation optimization.

papers.title: Assessing the Generalizability of Machine Learning and Physics-Based Methods with DNA-Encoded Libraries.
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-ligand binding is a central challenge in computational drug discovery, and while machine learning (ML) and cofolding methods have advanced rapidly, their ability to generalize beyond training or parametrization regimes remains insufficiently understood. DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) enable ultralarge screening of billions of molecules simultaneously, providing a useful testbed for evaluating these approaches at scale. A recent NeurIPS competition revealed that even top-performing ML models trained on DEL data failed at generalizing to out-of-distribution (OOD) chemical space.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper evaluates how well machine learning and physics-based protein-ligand binding prediction methods generalize beyond their training or parametrization regimes, using DNA-encoded library (DEL) data as a large-scale testbed. Building on a NeurIPS competition finding that top ML models trained on DEL data failed on out-of-distribution chemical space, the work probes the limits of current computational binding prediction approaches. The study highlights that strong in-distribution performance does not translate to reliable generalization.

papers.title: CUE: A Chemical Uncertainty-Aware Embedding Framework for Multimodal Drug Selectivity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug selectivity is critical for prioritizing candidate compounds with reduced off-target effects in AI-based drug discovery. Although selectivity can be inferred indirectly from drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction, cumulative errors from affinity predictions across multiple targets can reduce reliability, motivating the development of methods that directly predict compound-level selectivity. We propose a Chemical Uncertainty-aware Embedding (CUE) framework that integrates molecular fingerprints and 2D molecular structure image embeddings. The two modalities are combin
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: CUE is a multimodal framework that directly predicts compound-level drug selectivity by combining molecular fingerprints with 2D molecular structure image embeddings, rather than inferring selectivity indirectly from individual drug-target affinity predictions. The framework incorporates chemical uncertainty awareness to improve reliability, addressing the problem of cumulative errors that arise when selectivity is derived from multiple separate affinity predictions.

papers.title: AI Accelerated Chemical Screening Integrates ChemBERTa to Identify Repositionable CASP4 Inhibitors via MD Simulations and MM/PBSA Analysis.
papers.abstract: This study employed an integrated ligand-based virtual screening pipeline to identify potential CASP4 inhibitors from the DrugBank database, leveraging docking-score prioritization, SMILES-derived ChemBERTa embeddings, and key physicochemical descriptors. Building on this foundation, the workflow incorporated virtual screening, cheminformatics modeling, PK-PD evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA free-energy analysis to systematically prioritize repurposed DrugBank compounds for CASP4-targeted Alzheimer's disease therapy. A Random Forest classifier trained
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study combines ligand-based virtual screening with ChemBERTa (a chemical language model) embeddings and a Random Forest classifier to prioritize DrugBank compounds as potential CASP4 inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease. Hits were validated through docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA free-energy calculations, yielding repurposable candidate inhibitors. The work demonstrates an AI-accelerated drug-repurposing pipeline integrating chemical language models with physics-based simulation.

papers.title: TopoLIA: Topology-Inspired Latent Interaction Attention for Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: The growing sophistication of drug discovery calls for new advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Transformers have underpinned recent breakthroughs in AI, yet their conventional source-target attention mechanism can become a bottleneck for modeling complex interactions. Here, we introduce TopoLIA, a topology-inspired latent interaction attention mechanism that learns not only how much information should be exchanged between interaction partners, but also how that information should be transformed. Source-target-dependent attention is mediated through a compact latent interaction space, pro
papers.summary: TopoLIA introduces a new attention mechanism for transformer models that uses a compact latent interaction space to learn both how much information to exchange between interacting entities and how to transform it, addressing a bottleneck in standard source-target attention. This topology-inspired approach is designed for drug discovery applications, where modeling complex molecular interactions is critical. The work represents a methodological advance in AI for drug discovery, though its practical impact will depend on validation across diverse tasks.

papers.title: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) causes dengue fever, a globally prevalent, epidemic-prone disease with no FDA-approved antivirals. Additionally, the available vaccine for DENV can increase the risk of severe dengue fever for those who have never had a DENV infection due to antibody-dependent enhancement. Thus, there is an urgent need to identify DENV antivirals. Drug repurposing, high-content screening, and machine learning were leveraged to efficiently identify antivirals likely to inhibit DENV replication. Using high-content screening in a DENV infection model, we characterized the morphological pattern
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes a drug-repurposing screen that combines high-content morphological imaging with a pseudotime analysis framework to identify compounds that inhibit dengue virus replication. The approach uses machine learning to characterize infection-associated morphological changes and rank candidate antivirals from a repurposing library. It offers a scalable strategy for antiviral discovery against a virus with no approved therapeutics.

papers.title: An AI-Enabled Translational Drug Discovery Framework for NALCN Channelopathy: From High-Throughput Screening to Therapeutic Candidate.
papers.abstract: More than 90% of rare diseases lack an approved therapy, partly reflecting economic barriers in developing treatments for small patient populations. A common bottleneck is costly and resource-intensive hit-to-lead prioritization. Congenital contractures of the limbs and face, hypotonia, and developmental delay (CLIFAHDD) is an ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disease often caused by de novo gain-of-function variants in the sodium leak channel NALCN, with no approved treatments.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes an AI-enabled drug discovery pipeline for CLIFAHDD, an ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by gain-of-function mutations in the NALCN sodium leak channel. The framework spans high-throughput screening through hit-to-lead prioritization to identify a therapeutic candidate, aiming to reduce the cost and resource burden that typically blocks treatment development for ultra-rare diseases.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Integrated Proteome-Wide Target Prioritization for Drug Discovery against Multidrug-Resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
papers.abstract: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes ∼82.4 million infections annually and is rapidly approaching an untreatable status. The pathogen has developed resistance to every antibiotic class introduced since the sulfonamide era. Ceftriaxone, the last WHO- and CDC-recommended empirical therapy, is now compromised by high-level resistance in extensively drug-resistant lineages reported across multiple continents. No licensed vaccine exists, and no antibiotic with a novel mechanism has been introduced for this pathogen in over 40 years. Conventional drug discovery is too slow and insufficiently resistance-awar
papers.summary: The authors present an AI-integrated, proteome-wide pipeline to prioritize candidate drug targets in multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae, a pathogen that has become resistant to every antibiotic class and lacks a vaccine. By systematically ranking proteins across the whole proteome, the approach aims to accelerate resistance-aware target selection for a pathogen where conventional drug discovery has stalled for decades.

papers.title: Hybrid Mechanistic-Neural Modeling of Concentration-Time Dynamics Generalizes Human Pharmacokinetics Prediction Across Unseen Chemical Space.
papers.abstract: The pharmacokinetics concentration-time profile encodes ADME dynamics. Its optimization in drug discovery curbs late-stage attrition, yet forecasting human pharmacokinetics from chemical structure remains difficult. Machine learning models ignore continuous ADME dynamics, whereas physiologically based pharmacokinetics (PBPK) models demand unavailable parameters and impose rigid, misspecified compartmental structures. We present PK-MUSE ( P harmaco K inetic hybrid M echanistic U niversal S ystem E quation), augmenting a two-compartment model with bounded, state- and time-dependent neural correc
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PK-MUSE, a hybrid model that combines a two-compartment pharmacokinetic framework with neural network corrections to predict human concentration-time profiles directly from chemical structure. This approach outperforms purely mechanistic PBPK models and purely machine-learning models, and generalizes to unseen chemical space. The work suggests hybrid mechanistic-neural modeling can improve early-stage pharmacokinetic prediction in drug discovery.

papers.title: Drugging the Undruggable in Oncology: Structural Computation, Machine Learning, and Generative AI for Historically Intractable Targets.
papers.abstract: For four decades the central oncogenic drivers of human cancer the RAS GTPases, the transcription-factor MYC, mutant p53, and the protein-tyrosine phosphatases, fusion oncoproteins and intrinsically disordered regulators that surround them were regarded as undruggable: lacking deep, well-defined small-molecule binding pockets, governed by femtomolar substrate affinities, or driven through flat protein-protein interfaces that classical medicinal chemistry could not engage. The last decade has overturned that verdict. This narrative review argues that the convergence of three advances has made t
papers.summary: This narrative review argues that the long-standing notion of 'undruggable' cancer targets like RAS, MYC, and mutant p53 has been overturned by three converging advances: structural computation, machine learning, and generative AI. It surveys how these computational approaches are enabling drug discovery against targets previously considered intractable due to flat binding pockets or disordered interfaces.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Screening Bioactive Compounds in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Computational Prediction, Multi-Omics Integration, and Clinical Translation Potential.
papers.abstract: Identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) requires computational prioritization to be connected with chemical and pharmacological evidence. This structured narrative and critical review examines machine learning applications in compound prediction, formula-compatibility analysis, multi-omics integration, and drug development and repurposing. Molecular fingerprints, graph and sequence representations, knowledge graphs, and generative models are discussed in relation to their intended endpoints and validation conditions. Studies are classified along two independent di
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning approaches for identifying bioactive compounds in traditional Chinese medicine, covering molecular representations (fingerprints, graph and sequence models, knowledge graphs, generative models), formula-compatibility analysis, multi-omics integration, and drug repurposing. It critically classifies studies by their intended endpoints and validation conditions, emphasizing the need to connect computational predictions with chemical and pharmacological evidence. The authors also discuss the potential for clinical translation of these computational screening strategies.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in hepatitis: Advances in diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial i
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes how machine learning and deep learning are being applied to hepatitis care, including early diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognostic prediction. It highlights the potential of AI to integrate large, heterogeneous biomedical datasets to address unmet clinical needs in hepatology.

papers.title: A review on advances in chemical compound toxicology prediction.
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of chemical toxicity remains a major challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment because conventional approaches can be costly, time-consuming, ethically constrained, and limited in predictive performance. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is being applied to predictive toxicology. It covers conventional algorithms such as support vector machines (SVMs), decision trees (DTs), and ensemble methods, together with advanced approaches including graph neural networks (GNNs). The
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being applied to predict chemical toxicity, covering conventional algorithms like SVMs, decision trees, and ensembles alongside newer graph neural networks. It frames these methods as responses to the cost, time, ethical, and performance limits of traditional toxicity testing in drug development and chemical safety assessment.

papers.title: Establishing standardized evaluation protocols for peptide-target interaction prediction: the PTI-TAPE consensus framework eDelphi.
papers.abstract: Computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction has advanced rapidly as a tool for drug discovery, yet the field lacks agreed evaluation standards. Discrepancies in metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction across publications currently render cross-study comparisons methodologically intractable, ultimately impeding the clinical translation of therapeutic peptides. To resolve this, we present PTI-TAPE (Peptide-Target Interaction-Tasks Assessing Peptide Engagement), a standardised benchmarking framework developed via a structured three-round eDelphi consensus stu
papers.summary: The authors present PTI-TAPE, a consensus framework developed through a three-round eDelphi study to standardize how computational peptide-target interaction predictions are evaluated. It addresses inconsistencies in metrics, negative sampling, and dataset construction that currently make cross-study comparisons unreliable. The framework aims to enable more rigorous benchmarking and support clinical translation of therapeutic peptides.

papers.title: Computational identification of candidate biomarkers and compounds associated with skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity improvement mediated by physical activity: an integrative multi-omics and computational chemistry study.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) underlies many chronic diseases. While physical activity improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity (IS), the underlying molecular mechanisms and targeted drug strategies remain elusive. This hypothesis-generating study integrates bioinformatics and computational chemistry using public datasets; all findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates public multi-omics datasets with computational chemistry to identify candidate biomarkers and small-molecule compounds linked to physical-activity-mediated improvement of skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity. The authors propose molecular candidates and drug-like compounds as hypotheses for future experimental testing, but no wet-lab validation is reported.
